introHeading: The mirror booth, built for Williamsburg's rooftops and lofts
introParas: Williamsburg is the neighborhood where the mirror booth photographs best, and it isn't close. A rooftop on Wythe or Kent puts the Manhattan skyline directly behind the gold frame, and because the mirror reads at full height, a whole wedding party can pile into one frame with the skyline lit up behind them rather than squeezing three people into a phone shot. Behind the glass sits the same Canon DSLR and studio ring light we run everywhere, so the photo looks shot in a studio even with a rooftop doing the work in the background.

Rooftop setups come with real logistics, not just a nice view. Wind is the first thing we plan around — the mirror's touchscreen is a large flat surface, so we position it in a covered or wind-sheltered spot and secure it the way we would any tall equipment outdoors. We scout ceiling clearance and power with you before the date, since a Wythe Avenue roof deck and a private terrace off Kent Avenue rarely have the same electrical setup. When the party moves indoors instead — a corporate night in a converted warehouse off Berry Street, a milestone birthday in an East Williamsburg loft — the same booth travels up a freight elevator without trouble, since its footprint is built to clear in a single trip.

Setup takes about 20 minutes and we arrive a full hour ahead of your start time, so it's tested and quiet before your first guest walks in. The booth wants a 10ft x 10ft footprint with room for a backdrop and props table, though we can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter loft floor, and all it needs is a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet — worth confirming ahead of time if your venue is an older industrial building where circuits get shared fast. There is no travel fee anywhere in Williamsburg; it's minutes from us, and we quote everything from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Mirror Photo Booth in Williamsburg — FAQ

faqs.q: Does the mirror booth work on a Wythe or Kent Avenue rooftop?
faqs.a: Yes — it's one of our most-requested rooftop setups in the neighborhood. We need a level, wind-sheltered position since the touchscreen is a large flat surface, plus a spot out of direct sun so the screen doesn't wash out with glare. We'll scout ceiling access, elevator size and power with you before the date.

faqs.q: Can the mirror booth fit into a Berry Street or East Williamsburg loft using a freight elevator?
faqs.a: Yes. The booth's footprint is built to clear in a single freight-elevator trip, which is the standard load-in for most converted industrial spaces off Berry. Tell us if your building has an unusual turn or a walk-up and we'll confirm clearance before your date.

faqs.q: Do you charge extra to bring the mirror booth to Williamsburg?
faqs.a: No travel fee — Williamsburg is minutes from us. We quote everything from your venue ZIP code before you book, so there's nothing to discover on the invoice afterward.

faqs.q: Can guests sign or write on their photo at the mirror booth?
faqs.a: Yes. The touchscreen supports on-screen signatures and drawings, so guests can leave a message right on their print — a favorite at Williamsburg weddings where the couple keeps every strip in a guest book afterward.

faqs.q: Is the mirror booth still readable outdoors at dusk, when a rooftop's light is changing fast?
faqs.a: Yes. The mirror runs its own Canon DSLR and studio ring light rather than relying on ambient light, so the photo quality stays consistent as a Wythe or Kent rooftop moves from daylight into evening. The one thing we do avoid is direct, harsh sun, since that creates glare on the touchscreen glass.

faqs.q: How much space does the mirror booth need?
faqs.a: The optimal footprint is 10ft x 10ft, which leaves room for the backdrop, props table and a red carpet if you want one. We can compress to a minimum of 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter Williamsburg loft or rooftop bar, and we need one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with a Williamsburg mirror booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your Williamsburg rental — setup, keeping the prop table organized, helping guests use the touchscreen, and packing down at the end of the night.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you arrive early for a rooftop event?
faqs.a: Setup takes about 20 minutes once we're on site, and we arrive a full hour before your scheduled start time so everything is tested and quiet before guests arrive. If your rooftop or loft needs us there earlier for an access window, idle time runs $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Williamsburg venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we will send it over.

faqs.q: Which Williamsburg neighborhoods do you cover?
faqs.a: We're out across North Williamsburg, South Williamsburg, East Williamsburg, Wythe Avenue, Berry Street, Kent Avenue and the surrounding areas most weekends of the season. If your venue isn't on that list, ask anyway — we'll tell you honestly whether we can get there.
